planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Convexa is one of the oldest and most widely planted Japanese holly selections, named for its cupped, convex leaf shape.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun. Convexa is a dense, rounded, spreading selection that typically grows wider than tall, with small, glossy, distinctly convex (cupped) dark-green leaves that distinguish it from flatter-leaved Japanese holly cultivars. It tolerates shearing well and is a classic choice for informal or lightly clipped hedges, mass plantings, and foundation shrubs where a boxwood-like texture is wanted without boxwood blight risk. Established plants are tough and adaptable, tolerating heat, light shade, and a range of soils as long as drainage is adequate.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Golden Gem is a compact, male (non-fruiting) selection with foliage that turns gold in cooler months.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun. Golden Gem is a dwarf, spreading Japanese holly selection with small leaves that turn bright gold-yellow through the colder months and green up somewhat in summer, giving year-round interest without fruiting since it is an all-male clone. Its low, compact mounding habit suits edging, rock gardens, and mixed borders where a touch of color is wanted against darker evergreens. Keep soil consistently moist but well drained, since this slow-growing selection resents both drought stress and waterlogging.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Green Island forms a low, open, spreading mound useful as a boxwood-like groundcover shrub.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun. Green Island is a low, open, spreading Japanese holly selection with glossy, dark-green, slightly scalloped leaves, growing wider than tall and forming a loose mound rather than a tight dome. It works well as a low informal hedge, mass groundcover planting on slopes, or facer shrub in front of taller evergreens, and tolerates light shearing if a neater outline is desired.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Dwarf Pagoda is an extremely slow-growing, miniature selection prized for rock gardens and troughs.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun. Dwarf Pagoda is a true miniature Japanese holly with tiny, tightly congested leaves on short, stacked stems that give the plant a layered, pagoda-like look even without pruning. Growth is extremely slow, so it is best used in rock gardens, troughs, and small-space accent plantings rather than hedging, and needs little to no shearing to stay neat for years. Protect from harsh winter wind and provide consistent moisture with sharp drainage, since the dense, small-leaved habit can trap excess moisture against the stems.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Mariesii is an old, very slow-growing dwarf selection with tiny leaves on short, dense stems.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun. Mariesii is a long-grown dwarf Japanese holly selection with very small, closely spaced leaves and dense, slow, compact growth, reaching only modest size even after many years in the ground. Its fine texture and tidy habit suit rock gardens, trough plantings, and small foundation beds where a full-size shrub would quickly outgrow the space. Little pruning is needed; just keep soil evenly moist and well drained and shelter from drying winter wind.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Beehive forms a naturally dense, flattened-globe shape developed as a compact, low-maintenance selection.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun. Beehive is a dense, naturally rounded, slightly flattened-globe Japanese holly selection with small, glossy deep-green leaves that holds its tidy shape with minimal shearing. It is well suited to foundation plantings, low formal hedges, and mass groupings where a uniform, compact evergreen form is wanted without constant pruning upkeep. Provide consistently moist, well-drained, acidic soil and light shade in hot climates for best appearance.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Jersey Pinnacle is a fast-growing, upright pyramidal selection bred at Rutgers University.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun. Jersey Pinnacle grows into a dense, upright, pyramidal form with broad, deep-green leaves, filling in faster than many other Japanese holly selections and giving good screening or vertical structure without the extreme narrowness of columnar types like Sky Pencil. It works well as an unclipped informal screen, corner accent, or narrow hedge, tolerating light shearing if a crisper outline is wanted. Keep soil evenly moist and well drained, and provide some afternoon shade in hot summer climates.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Rotundifolia is an old, vigorous selection with rounded leaves and an upright, dense habit traditionally used for hedging.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun. Rotundifolia is one of the older, larger-growing Japanese holly selections, with rounded, leathery leaves and a dense, upright-to-rounded habit that has long made it a staple hedging plant in the trade. It tolerates regular shearing well and is often grown as a sheared hedge or large foundation mass where a tougher, more vigorous grower than the small dwarf cultivars is wanted. Provide consistently moist, well-drained, acidic soil, and expect a faster-filling, larger plant than compact selections like Helleri or Compacta.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Oamacha is a traditional Japanese cultivar whose sweet leaves were historically dried to brew ama-cha tea.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, ideally with morning sun and afternoon shelter from harsh afternoon heat. Oamacha is a compact, bushy mountain hydrangea bearing flattened lacecap flowerheads of white to pink (or blue in acidic soil) from early to midsummer, with foliage that develops attractive purplish tones into autumn. Its sweet-tasting leaves were traditionally dried and used to brew a sweet Japanese tea, a practice behind the cultivar's name. Keep soil consistently moist but well drained, and mulch to protect roots from summer heat and winter cold swings.
